labelOrigin: Each label was written from the fix commit's message and diff before the checker was run on either revision. siteLines are lines of the buggy (parent) revision: the queueing call and the access or lifetime end it races with.
matching: A case is found when the parent revision has a CL1-CL4 diagnostic whose primary location or any code-flow location in the labelled file is on one of siteLines; the fix silences it when the fixed revision has no such diagnostic.

cases.bug: set_element_async copies the block-scoped host variable single_node to the device asynchronously; the block ends, and the variable with it, before the copy is known to have read it.
A host staging vector is copied to the device with cuda_memcpy_async and destroyed when the function returns, without synchronizing the stream.
The constructor queues an asynchronous copy from the caller's string storage into a device buffer and returns; the caller may destroy or change the string before the copy reads it.
A block-scoped pinned host vector is copied to the device with make_device_uvector_async and destroyed at the end of the block while the copy may be pending.
The host buffer holding the flattened regex program is copied with cuda_memcpy_async and destroyed when the function returns, without synchronizing the stream.
Each Arrow host chunk is released right after from_arrow queued copies from it (cudaMemcpyBatchAsync on CUDA 13), before the stream has executed them.
A pinned staging slot is overwritten with memcpy for a new dispatch while an earlier cuMemcpyHtoDAsync from the same slot may not have read it; the slots form a ring reused across calls.

merge_lists makes the allocating stream wait on the donor stream's event but does not re-record the allocating stream's event, so later waits on that event no longer cover the donor stream's in-flight work.
A blocking cudaMemcpy H2D into a device tensor returns before work on other streams can rely on the data; the fix adds a device synchronize so later kernels see it.
cases.outsideRules: device-side ordering of an ordinary device buffer between streams

cases.bug: A device-to-device copy between two backends on the same device is queued on the destination stream instead of the source stream, so it is not ordered after the source's producer work.
cases.outsideRules: device-side ordering of ordinary device buffers between streams

cases.bug: On devices without concurrent managed access (WSL), the host runs atomics on managed or system memory while the kernel launched just before may still be using it.
cases.outsideRules: host access to managed or system-allocated memory used by a kernel

cases.bug: A device buffer written by a just-launched kernel is passed to CUDA-aware MPI_Send without synchronizing.
cases.outsideRules: a device buffer with pending kernel work passed to a library call (recorded as a coverage gap, not reported)

cases.bug: A cudaMemcpy with cudaMemcpyDefault stages data that the NIC or MPI then reads; the fix synchronizes the default stream before handing the buffer over.
cases.outsideRules: device-side completion of a copy consumed by a NIC outside CUDA
